problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14108214/assets/e2591e9da960008980cf96184975ef19713735814183a97ca8c8f784536fced5.png)

Describe the shaded region shown above using set-builder notation.

$$
{(x,y)\in {{field-1}}\,:\,-x-3\,{{field-2}}\,y\,{{field-3}}\,x+4}
$$
worked_solution:
The points in our set include all those that lie *above* the line $y=-x-3$ and *below* the line $y=x+4.$

A point $P(x,y)$ lies *inside* the shaded region if the following conditions are satisfied:

$$
y>-x-3,\,y<x+4.
$$

 

Combining this into a single condition, we have

$$
-x-3<y<x+4.
$$

We must also include the lines $y=-x-3$ and $y=x+4$ since the boundaries are included in the set (the lines are solid). So, we change the corresponding inequality symbols above as follows:

$$
-x-3\le y\le x+4
$$

Moreover, since we're considering *every* real value in this region, $x\in R,y\in R,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in R\times R={R}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, we can write the set as

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,-x-3\le y\le x+4}.
$$
